node.label: Desmond Morton
node.date_label: Working People (with Terry Copp) (1980) · Winning the Second Battle (with Glenn T. Wright) (1987) · When Your Number’s Up (1993)
node.description: Canadian historian who connected military institutions and soldiers’ experience with social and labour history. John Bullen reads Working People as a synthesis linking labour disputes and political organization, while Morton’s own2018 recollections interpret war remembrance through national formation. These placements describe different strands of his writing; coauthors Terry Copp and Glenn T. Wright retain their credit.

proposed_edges.relationship: Working People (1980, with Terry Copp) synthesizes labour conflict and organization within Canadian political development.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: John Bullen’s1981 opening assessment supports this contribution; no sole authorship or claim to inaugurate labour history.

proposed_edges.relationship: Morton’s writing and remembrance interpret soldiers’ wartime experience within Canadian nation formation.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: His quoted2018 interpretation of Vimy and his family’s remembrance supplies an own-voice example; national coming-of-age remains his contested interpretive position.
